summary: Register-only cold review of the Christ the King 1962 homily (homily.tex, sections/homily/10-homily.tex read straight through as heard, 90-note.tex for leakage), judged against guidance/editorial.md 'Say what the texts say, plainly', the version-14 review and homily-review fragments, and the three-document profile's homily section. Source verification, citations, timing and layout were not checked by this dispatch. The speech's teaching content is sound and much of it is plain narration and attributed exposition, but the defects the 21 October 2026 register remediation named are still present and recur: maxim and paradox closers end most paragraphs (including the exact 'There is no Monday outside his kingdom' sentence the standard cites), a 'Monday' tag and slogan, two relatable inventories, the forbidden stock call 'take one thing out of this church' with the 'This week, choose one place' formula, repeated restatement of just-quoted texts, and performed emphasis ('listen', 'From hence.', 'Think what follows.') with self-answered questions. Four recurring patterns are blocking; isolated asserted significance, foil denials, inferences credited to texts, and apparatus vocabulary in the note are advisory. Quoted liturgical, biblical and patristic text, Augustine's of/in and here/hence antitheses, the opening Gospel question, and the final Introit acclamation were not faulted. Verdict: CHANGES_REQUIRED.

findings.problem: Maxim, paradox and chiasmus closers recur through the speech: paragraph after paragraph ends one sentence late on an aphorism that restates or ornaments what the paragraph has already said. Instances: 59-60 'That is how a bound prisoner can claim the whole earth. There is no Monday outside his kingdom.' (the exact sentence guidance/editorial.md names as the defect); 72-73 'We were not conquered into this kingdom. We were carried into it.'; 94 'The Lamb is worthy because he was slain.'; 99-100 'The wound the Collect named is healed at this altar.'; 102-103 'The first good it names is the truth the prisoner was born to bear witness to.'; 113-114 'That is our first place in this kingdom.'; 123-124 'Christ's kingdom takes no one's throne from him. It tells him for whom he holds it.'; 135 'We fight with the King's own weapons in Pilate's hall: the truth, patience, and a life given up.'; 151-152 'The throne of heaven and the throne in a faithful heart belong to one King.'; 161-162 'His kingdom is not from hence, and so there is nowhere it does not reach.' The delete-the-last-sentence test loses nothing in each case except the cadence.
findings.required_result: End each paragraph where its information ends; cut the closer rather than polishing it, and keep any real content as a plain statement. For example: (a) 55-60: end on Aquinas, 'St Thomas Aquinas puts it simply: it is not from here, and yet it is here, because it is everywhere.' and delete 'That is how a bound prisoner can claim the whole earth. There is no Monday outside his kingdom.' (b) 70-73: 'St Paul, in the Epistle, gave thanks to the Father who "hath translated us into the kingdom of the Son of his love." To translate is to carry over: the Father has brought us into the kingdom.' and delete the conquered/carried pair. (c) 122-124: end on Bellarmine's '"kings were created for the people, not the people for kings."' and delete the two closing sentences. (d) 150-152: end on Schuster's 'Jesus is enthroned in the faithful heart' and delete 'The throne of heaven and the throne in a faithful heart belong to one King.' (e) 161-162: the final paragraph does not restate the thesis of 57-59; delete 'His kingdom is not from hence, and so there is nowhere it does not reach.'

findings.problem: Unearned homiletic devices the three-document profile excludes run through the speech. (1) A recurring tag, 'Monday': 43 'Then Monday comes, with the office, the household and the ballot box'; 60 'There is no Monday outside his kingdom.'; 160-161 'Give him your Monday as well as your Sunday.' (a slogan; the note itself, 90-note.tex:57, lists 'the Monday outside no kingdom' as the homily's own join). No appointed text mentions the week; the tag is the speech's own refrain. (2) Relatable inventories of the listeners' lives: 42-43 'in heaven, in the soul, in this church for an hour on Sunday ... the office, the household and the ballot box'; 117-119 'a household, a classroom, a ward through the night, a vote'. (3) The stock call and the very formula the profile records as the failure of both providers' Christ the King homilies: 137-138 'So take one thing out of this church. This week, choose one place where you hold some authority, however small.' (the profile names 'take one thing out of this church' verbatim as a forbidden stock call). (4) A refrain built around it: the response repeats Jn 18:37 already quoted at 69 ('Ask whose voice you are hearing. "Every one that is of the truth heareth my voice."' 140-141, again 'Be of the truth, and hear his voice' 160), and 'Ask for whom you hold it' (139) re-sounds 124 'It tells him for whom he holds it'.
findings.required_result: Keep one practicable response drawn from the text, said once in ordinary words, with no stock call, inventory, tag or slogan. For example: (a) replace 137-141 with 'Anyone who holds authority over others can pray the Introit's verse before using it: "Give to the king thy judgment, O God, and to the king's son thy justice."' (b) 117-119: 'Most of us wear no crown, but many of us hold some authority over others, and Augustine's second place belongs to it.' (no list of offices). (c) 40-44: state the misunderstanding once without the Monday/ballot-box inventory, e.g. 'We can hear "My kingdom is not of this world" as meaning that Christ is King only in heaven or in the soul, and that the rest of life belongs to some other king.' (d) 160-161: delete 'Give him your Monday as well as your Sunday.' and 60's Monday sentence (see HOM-REG-001), so the motif is gone.

findings.problem: The speech repeatedly paraphrases what the listener has just heard. 50 'The words tell us where the kingdom comes from, not where it is.' then 52-53 'It is here; it is not from here.' both restate Augustine's quotation at 51-52 immediately before and after it; 69-70 'It is entered by hearing.' restates the verse 'Every one that is of the truth heareth my voice' just quoted; 93 'The kingdom is his by birth.' restates 86 'Christ was born a King, as Chrysostom insists.'; 161-162 restates the thesis of 57-59 as a closing summary. The pattern recurs across three movements.
findings.required_result: Say each thing once. For example: (a) 49-53: '... He said, "my kingdom is not from hence." "For His kingdom is here until the end of the world," Augustine says, "having tares intermingled therewith until the harvest. ... It only sojourns as a stranger in the world."' with 'From hence. The words tell us where the kingdom comes from, not where it is.' and 'It is here; it is not from here.' deleted. (b) 92-94: 'The kingdom is his by birth. As man, he wins the nations ...' becomes 'As man, he wins the nations in that hall, by the passion that has begun.' (c) 69-70: delete 'It is entered by hearing.' and let the Epistle sentence follow the verse.

findings.problem: Performed emphasis recurs instead of emphasis from content: 46 'But listen to what he actually says. St Augustine noticed what is easy to miss.' ('listen', and an announcement of insight); 50 'From hence.' (an emphatic fragment, the example the editorial standard names); 55 'Think what follows.' (named verbatim in the standard); 75 'but hear how'; 109 'Look again at the Gradual's kings.' Alongside them, questions the speaker poses and answers in the next breath: 64 'Then how does such a kingdom take hold of anyone?' (answered at once by the verse); 107 'What, then, does this King ask of us?' (answered at once); 130 'So what is this fight? It is not his defence; he needs none.' (82 and 89 are left aside: there the question is answered by the Father who raises it, Chrysostom and Aquinas, which is proper; 35-36 is the question the Gospel raises and is worked out over the following paragraphs, also proper.)
findings.required_result: Remove the announcements and the self-answered questions; let the source or text speak. For example: (a) 46-49: 'St Augustine points to the words the Lord uses. He did not say, my kingdom is not in this world, but not of this world; and he did not say, my kingdom is not here, but "my kingdom is not from hence."' (b) 55: delete 'Think what follows.' and begin 'A kingdom that comes from one place in the world is bounded by that place.' (c) 75-78: 'The Collect asked that the nations be subjected to Christ. It calls them nations "separated by the wound of sin", and the rule it asks for is "His most loving dominion."' (d) 130-133: 'St Hilary says that the kingdom of God is where sin is overcome and death destroyed; the fight of this prayer is against sin.' in place of the question and its denial. (e) 107: drop the question and open the paragraph on Augustine's reading of the Gradual's kings.

findings.problem: Asserted significance: 'puts to him the question on which this whole feast turns.' is the form the editorial standard names ('the words on which the feast turns'). Isolated in the speech.
findings.required_result: State the scene: 'so Pilate goes in to the prisoner, bound since his arrest in the garden, and asks him whether he is a king.' or simply end the sentence at 'puts to him the question.'

findings.problem: Denials of positions no source or listener puts forward: 72 'We were not conquered into this kingdom.'; 96 'That sacrifice is not behind us.'; 112-113 'The king who adores Christ does not stand above the poor. He kneels among them' (Augustine's text, quoted at 111-112, puts the kings in the believing people; the 'does not stand above' half is the speech's foil). 123 ('takes no one's throne from him') and 130-131 ('It is not his defence') answer a worry the Gospel or a reasonable listener could bring and are not counted. 72 is also an HOM-REG-001 closer.
findings.required_result: State the positive claim. 96: 'In the Secret, the prayer said quietly over the gifts, the priest will offer "this host for the reconciliation of humanity" ...' without 'That sacrifice is not behind us.' 112-114: 'The king who adores Christ kneels among the poor and confesses his sins.'

findings.problem: The homily's own links between texts are stated as what the texts or the altar do, though the note (90-note.tex:56-58) records them as the homily's own and credited to no Father: 99-100 'The wound the Collect named is healed at this altar.' joins Collect to Secret as fact; 102-103 'The first good it names is the truth the prisoner was born to bear witness to.' ties the Preface's word order to Jn 18:37 as though the Preface drew the link. Both also close their paragraphs (HOM-REG-001).
findings.required_result: State such a link once as an inference or drop it: 'and ask that Christ bestow on all the nations "the gifts of unity and peace" — unity, we may say, for the nations the Collect called separated by the wound of sin.' For 102-103, end on the Preface's own words.

findings.problem: Register leaks into the unspoken apparatus. The note calls the study's interpretations 'readings' ('Relation to the reviewed readings' 29, 'the second of the full study's three readings' 30, 'From the first reading' 44, 'From the third reading' 51), which in a homily's note collides directly with the Mass's own readings (Epistle and Gospel; 'the first reading' is ordinarily the Epistle). 56-57 'These joins are the homily's own ...: the Monday outside no kingdom' uses production vocabulary ('joins') and the speech's tag as if the reader shared it. The PDF subject in homily.tex:8 repeats the paradox slogan 'a kingdom not of this world and not from hence and therefore everywhere'.
findings.required_result: Write 'the study's three interpretations' / 'the second interpretation' (or name each by its title alone) and 'These connections are the homily's own'; describe the speech's application plainly rather than by its tag; give the PDF subject as a plain description of the homily's content.
